segments.speaker: ROB
segments.en: Good morning. Stretton Festival box office. How can I help you?

segments.speaker: MELANIE
segments.en: Oh, hello. My family and I are on holiday on the area, and we’ve seen some posters about the festival this week. Could you tell me about some of the events, please?

segments.speaker: ROB
segments.en: Of course.

segments.speaker: MELANIE
segments.en: First of all, are there still tickets available for the jazz band on Saturday?

segments.speaker: ROB
segments.en: There are, but only £18 . The £12 seats have all been sold.

segments.speaker: MELANIE
segments.en: OK. And the venue is the school, isn’t it?

segments.speaker: ROB
segments.en: Yes, that’s right, the secondary school [[ ]] . Make sure you don’t go to the primary school by mistake! And there’s an additional performer who isn’t mentioned on the posters – Carolyn Hart is going to play with the band.

segments.speaker: MELANIE
segments.en: Oh, I think I’ve heard her on the radio. Doesn’t she play the oboe, or flute or something?

segments.speaker: ROB
segments.en: Yes the flute [[ ]] . She usually plays with symphony orchestras, and apparently this is her first time with a jazz band.

segments.speaker: MELANIE
segments.en: Well, I’d certainly like to hear her. Then the next thing I want to ask about is the duck races – I saw a poster beside a river. What are they, exactly?

segments.speaker: ROB
segments.en: Well, you buy a yellow plastic duck – or as many as you like – they’re a pound each. And you write your name on each one. There’ll be several races, depending on the number of ducks taking part. And John Stevens, a champion swimmer who lives locally, is going to start the races. All the ducks will be launched into the river at the back of the cinema [[ ]] , then they’ll float along the river for 500 metres, as far as the railway bridge.

segments.speaker: MELANIE
segments.en: And are there any prizes?

segments.speaker: ROB
segments.en: Yes, the first duck in each race to arrive at the finishing line wins its owner free tickets for the concert on the last night of the festival. [[ ]]

segments.speaker: MELANIE
segments.en: You said you can buy a duck? I’m sure my children will both want one.

segments.speaker: ROB
segments.en: They’re on sale at a stall in the market [[ ]] . You can’t miss it – it’s got an enormous sign showing a couple of ducks.

segments.speaker: MELANIE
segments.en: OK. I’ll go there this afternoon. I remember walking past there yesterday. Now could you tell me something about the flower show, please?

segments.speaker: ROB
segments.en: Well, admission is free, and the show is being held in Bythwaite Hall. [[ ]]

segments.speaker: MELANIE
segments.en: Sorry, how do you spell that?

segments.speaker: ROB
segments.en: B-Y-T-H-W-A-I-T-E. Bythwaite.

segments.speaker: MELANIE
segments.en: Is it easy to find? I’m no very familiar with the town yet.

segments.speaker: ROB
segments.en: Oh, you won’t have any problem. It’s right in the centre of Stretton. It’s the only old building in the town, so it’s easy to recognise.

segments.speaker: MELANIE
segments.en: I know it. I presume it’s open all day.

segments.speaker: ROB
segments.en: Yes, but if you’d like to see the prizes being awarded for the best flowers, you’ll need to be there at 5 o’clock. The prizes are being given by a famous actor, Kevin Shapless [[ ]] . He lives nearby and gets involved in a lot of community events.

segments.speaker: MELANIE
segments.en: Gosh, I’ve seen him on TV. I’ll definitely go to the prize-giving.

segments.speaker: MELANIE
segments.en: I’ve seen a list of plays that are being performed this week, and I’d like to know which are suitable for my children, and which ones my husband and I might go to.

segments.speaker: ROB
segments.en: How old are your children?

segments.speaker: MELANIE
segments.en: Five and seven. What about ‘The Mystery of Muldoon’?

segments.speaker: ROB
segments.en: That’s aimed at five to ten-year-olds. [[ ]]

segments.speaker: MELANIE
segments.en: So if I take my children, I can expect them to enjoy it more than I do?

segments.speaker: ROB
segments.en: I think so. If you’d like something for yourself and your husband and leave your children with a babysitter, you might like to see ‘Fire and Flood’ [[ ]] – it’s about events that really happened in Stretton two hundred years ago, and children might find it rather frightening.

segments.speaker: MELANIE
segments.en: Oh, thanks for the warning. And finally, what about ‘Silly Sailor’?

segments.speaker: ROB
segments.en: That’s a comedy, and it’s for young and old [[ ]] . In fact, it won an award in the Stretton Drama Festival a couple of months ago.

segments.speaker: MELANIE
segments.en: OK. Well, goodbye, and thanks for all the information. I’m looking forward to the festival!

segments.speaker: ROB
segments.en: Goodbye.
